chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Musa ibn Bakr from Ali ibn Sa'id said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the night prayer and the witr prayer during travel, from the beginning of the night, if one is unable to pray in the latter part. He said, 'Yes.'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And whoever is weak from standing in prayer, let him pray it sitting, up to his saying, 'And it is permissible for the patient (ill one).'
ai.seo_question: When can one perform night prayer and Witr during travel if unable to pray later?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) clarifies the flexibility of Salat al-Layl and Witr for travelers and the ill, permitting performance at the start of the night if the latter part is unfeasible. It further establishes the principle of *rukhas* (dispensations), allowing those physically unable to stand to pray while seated, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (*yusr*) in worship.
